title: Built this Helicopter Rescue Simulatot demo for $250 with ChatGPT Astra 6 and Unity. Sould i keep going ?
author: Huge_Veterinarian572
selftext: The goal is to recreate my home base at Birrfeld and fly helicopter missions all across Switzerland. After spending $250 in credits and hitting the limit, this is where I'm at: I can fly with a joystick, and everything from Zurich to Bern is visualized in 3D. Of course it's not finished yet, and a lot still needs tweaking. I'll pick it back up on Saturday. If anyone wants to help test it, send me a message!

replies.author: Huge_Veterinarian572
replies.body:
simulator is built in **Unity with URP**, combining several geographic sources:  
**Google Maps Platform – Photorealistic 3D Tiles:** the main photogrammetric environment.  
**Cesium for Unity / Cesium ion:** streams the geographic tiles and manages their detail levels.  
**swisstopo – swissBUILDINGS3D:** additional Swiss building geometry, currently partly using representative facade materials.  
**OpenStreetMap:** road and railway geometry for our simulated traffic.

comments.author: Proud_Ask_9030
comments.body:
If you want it improved, Ask it to:  
\-simulate the air pressure in an SDF that parametrically adjusts with the wind speed and direction and ground effects(main and tail rotors). Build telemetry and autopilot testing system to match real world data(nasa has plenty to use for the uh-60 and others)  
\- build a volumetric engine for ground effects(depending on surface material and collective) and engine exhaust(refraction heat effect and smoke)  
\-simulate realistic cyclic and collective controls so that player controls are semi autonomous(so they dont override the real controls limits and dynamics) and partly automate-assist RPM/pedals/hover.  
\-build the rigging so the rotors are fully articulated and connected with flight controls. Build a rotor fade system to emulate real visuals of rotor RPM fade. Adjust the main rotors so they flex to emulate the cyclic/collective changes to the rotors.

The problem is tech bros think that outsourcing to AI is the same as to a person. Its far from the truth. It doesn't replace people. Many studies have shown that in trying to do so its literally a Zero Sum Gain. You literally gain nothing. So why not gain knowledge so you can instruct to build beter systems, or understand whats going on, and have the ability to expand the technology.

People do enjoy assembling and working on cars. I know people that do this for hobby. 

Results dont always matter. The Journey is typically more valuable. Knowing how something works allows for you to change the way it works and make it better, add flare to it and change it and add something to make it better. Disconnecting from that means you are no longer creating. You might as well be a ceo that buys tesla and goes I invented electric cars. Its a joke.

And if your outsourcing your just taking advantage of something, your not doing it yourself and its just gross. Normalizing taking advantage of cheap labor, or from a machine that has stolen from artists and creatives is not ok.

Exactly. The tech debt. If your developing it by saying "add air pressure".  then your going to have tech debt. AI doesn't care that the air pressure feature cannot be expanded. It doesnt care that now it breaks x feature that was already developed.

also the lack of understanding to go in and fix whatever it writes is gonna be the fun thing to fix at the end of the project. Or it just wont and itll end up being something very sloppy and copy past nobody cares to play.

Any expert in a field using AI in there field sees the flaws in what AI generates. People that dont undetand the discipline fail to see the flaws ai tends to create. replies.author: Willy757
replies.body:
People on here are deluted lol.

Games are about having good tooling and parametrized code and fiddling with it for 100 iterations until the result is actually fun. When the game involves physics, the process is even more harsh.  

I've written code for vehicle simulators that takes 3 numbers: lift coeficient, drag coeficient, engine impulse. And I've written complicated surface simulations. One was bland and barely customizable, the other oppened up a whole world of posiblity.  Vibe coders will create the easier sistem first because that's what the bot prefers, add all the other features around it, then deside on a new detail like "what if one of the helocopter's wings falls off" and then half the code in the project will be irrelevant.  

Downvote me if you like. People who start projects and can't even be bothered to search relevant teqniques related to their final objective, people who just go "I want this and this and this 200 times in a row" will never launch a game that won't be review bombed. And Astra or any other bot will never be able to compensate for your own uninformed vision about what you want to do and achieve.
